items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy raised national security concerns. The company named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO.

items.headline: U.S. envoys meet Putin, then Zelenskyy
items.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow for about two hours on efforts to end the war in Ukraine. They then traveled to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

items.headline: Brooklyn building collapse kills 8
items.summary: A building collapse in Brooklyn killed eight people, including two children, New York City's mayor said. Dozens were injured, and officials ended rescue operations after finding no more victims.

items.headline: Holscher wins Kansas governor's race
items.summary: Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor's race over Republican Ty Masterson. Her win extends a wave of Democratic victories in the midterm elections.

items.headline: USDA proposes tighter SNAP eligibility
items.summary: The Agriculture Department proposed a change it says could remove about 6.3 million people from SNAP eligibility by fiscal 2029. That would come on top of 5.5 million people who recently lost benefits.

items.headline: Indonesia's vice president resigns
items.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, resigned. Courts had ruled that his overseas education documents did not meet election requirements.

items.headline: Spain holds first general strike in 14 years
items.summary: Millions of Spanish workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years. The walkout comes amid a housing crisis in Spain.

items.headline: Atmospheric rivers drench Pacific Northwest
items.summary: A series of atmospheric rivers is bringing heavy rain to Washington and Oregon. The storms are arriving alongside high tides and strong winds.

items.headline: Turnout shifts reshaped Deep South races
items.summary: An NPR analysis attributes a leftward shift in six Deep South states in the midterms to high Black voter turnout. Lower turnout in Republican-heavy areas also contributed.

items.headline: Google to cut Search for AI-free schools
items.summary: Google plans to cut off Search access for schools that opt out of its AI Overviews. The move has frustrated some parents and educators.

digest.overview:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO after reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and CFO Colette Kress became interim chief. Democrat Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor's race, while an Alaska judge rejected Mary Peltola's request for data on rejected absentee ballots as counting continues. Sen. Chris Van Hollen said he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. The Agriculture Department proposed SNAP changes it says could cut about 6.3 million people from eligibility by 2029. The House passed a bill raising compensation for combat-injured, medically retired veterans, sending it to the Senate. A Brooklyn building collapse killed eight people, including two children. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave a medal to a Tomb of the Unknown Soldier sentinel who had criticized his conduct. Atmospheric rivers are drenching Washington and Oregon.

Abroad, U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow and then Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin, with major differences on territory and security guarantees still unresolved. A confidential IAEA report said the agency cannot verify the status of Iran's Isfahan enrichment plant, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S. radar in Bahrain. North Korea's foreign minister rejected a G7 call for denuclearization. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed a crackdown on stock manipulation ahead of the ASEAN and APEC summits. Taiwan officials said China massed more than 100 vessels in unannounced Pacific drills. Indonesia's vice president resigned over questions about his education credentials. Millions of Spanish workers staged the first general strike in 14 years. At COP31 in Antalya, negotiators split over emissions cuts, climate finance and fossil fuels.

home.overview:
Detroit's Cade Cunningham poured in 52 points as the Pistons outlasted Washington 144–140 in double overtime, the highest-scoring game of the season, while Minnesota crushed Dallas 133–94 and Philadelphia beat Toronto 123–112 to reach 10-3. NBA Cup group play tips off tonight with nine games, including Knicks at Pacers and Warriors at Spurs. In the NFL, Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left gave Washington a 24–21 win at the Giants, who still lead the NFC East at 5-3-1; Sunday brings Patriots-Lions in Munich and Steelers-Bengals at night. Baseball handed out its top awards: Pete Crow-Armstrong and Yordan Alvarez were unanimous MVPs, and Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler won the Cy Youngs.

Harry Kane marked his record 126th England cap with the winning penalty in a 2–1 Nations League win over Croatia, Italy beat France 3–1 with two goals from Francesco Pio Esposito, and Spain won 2–0 in Czechia to set up Sunday's group decider against England in Madrid. Germany visit Serbia tonight, South Korea meet Saudi Arabia in Doha, and the USMNT face Haiti on Saturday amid reports that Mauricio Pochettino is headed to Manchester United. Club football, K League and the MLS playoffs return next week. In the KBO, Korean Series MVP Koo Ja-wook has hired a U.S. agent to pursue a major league deal.
